The job was simple, Neil was going to be filing and doing general administrative jobs for the project management office. A glorified errand boy for people who knew far less about construction than Neil did.
Neil guessed they’d thought with his experience, he’d know his way around organising all the plans, manifests, quotes and surveys large construction projects would have. Thet weren’t wrong, he be able to the job with his eyes closed, and perhaps with a bit of spare time he could figure a way of getting out as quickly as possible.
He was one of five assistants to the project office, Knox had introduced him to all of them, but Neil has already forgotten thier names. Knox himself wasn’t one of them, he worked in different department completely.
Right on time the bus arrived at the stop, 6:30pm, the sun was setting in the late summer heat and everyone piled onto the bus. It was a different crowd, he only recognised a few faces. 
Neil sat and scanned the faces getting on he was relieved when he didn’t see Rook get on. 
Tully from the morning bus ride sat next to Neil, he hadn’t realised just how large Tully was in the morning, he was as tall as Neil, but he must have been at least 240 pounds of muscle.
Tully extended his hand “Hi, names Tully, didn’t catch yours this morning”
Neil accepted the handshake, it was a more gentle than he expected, the faint smell of oil and grease in grained in Tully’s hand hit Neil’s nose “Neil, good to meet you”
Tully asked “They’ve got you over in Stratum Projects, very cushy, everyone wants an office job” he spread his hands wide for Neil to see, the black line under his nails made it clear he got dirty for his job “How’d you swing that?”
Neil shook his head “I have absolutely no idea”
Tully laughed “I have a feeling you’ll find out soon enough… now if you don’t mind I’m going to get some shut eye, us factory workers don’t get to sit down all day in air-conditioned comfort”
Neil wanted to ask what Tully meant, but it was clear the conversation was over, he sat in silence for the rest of the ride, Tully softly snoring beside him.</span></span></span></span>

The pot didn’t provide any cover really, it was only a foot tall and empty. 
Jim gently tilted it and felt under the pot, where was this key? His hand couldn’t find it so he tipped the pot further and bent over to look under.
There it was, stuck to the bottom of the pot with the dirt, it had been a while since he’d needed to use it. Jim grabbed for the key, the pot tipped over too far and he lost control of it. It clattered over and smashed into a dozen or so pieces.
No! The noise sounded deafening to Jim crouched on his knees in the quiet at the side of his house. Panicked he looked up and through the fence. It felt like the media turned as one to look towards the house, the low hum of mundane conversation of the bored media pack rose a pitch. Someone trained a spotlight to where the sound had come from. Jim could see the zebra petter of light and shadow on the ground and him.
He held deathly still, perhaps they couldn’t see him.
A voice yelled out “There’s someone there!” 
Shit, it was a that moment he realised he didn’t have the key in his hand, it was somewhere under the debris of the broken pot and the soil that it held now spread over the side path.
cameramen and reporters were now in a mad dash to his side gate with reporters and camera operators elbowing each other out of the way to get the best shots.
Jim was frantically pushing the broken pieces of terracotta around trying to find the key, he cut his hand on one of the shards and started adding his own blood to the soil.
The first camera man got to the gate stopped to leaned his camera over it and get the shot, but the gate opened and he fell into onto the path directly in front of Jim. Now the gate was open, the pack rushed in with not regard for Jim or the cameraman on the ground.
Jim was light up be a dozen camera mounted lights and the reporters were screaming questions at him at the same time
“Mr Dalton are you a member of the Greys?’
“Mr Dalton why did you assault the waitress?”
“Are you a danger to society”
“What’s it like being designated a disruptive Person?”
Jim’s hand found the key finally and he stood up, his pants covered in mud and dirt, his had red with blood, he eyes squinting starting into the lights.
The throng had surrounded him and were jostling him like he was in a washing machine, he had no choice but to push through them to get to the side door if his house.
Jim pushed but they didn’t move, he pushed again but they were shoulder to should in the tight space.
Jim yelled at them “Get out of my way, get off my property!” and pushed through again. He was hit in the face by one microphone, then another .
A cameraman had backed up into the doorway and Jim yelled again “Move!”
He didn’t.
Jim needed to get inside.
He grabbed cameraman and shoved him are hard as he could off the small stoop of the side door. The man went sprawling into the narrow garden between the side path and the house. His camera flew off onto the pathway smashing into pieces, all the other camera’s capturing the moment the man and the camera hit the ground.
Jim didn’t have time to see any of that, he showed the key into the lock and burst into house slamming the door shut behind him with a force that rattled the windows.
Jim collapsed onto the floor exhausted, he was spent, he didn’t even register the banging on the door as the adrenalin left his body and he passed out lying there on the cold floor in his dark house.</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">He see the news outside the house calling for his arrest for assault and damage to property, replaying the footage him pushing over the journalists.
He see’s the Police turn up to the front of his building, they call his apartment and tell him to stay where he is.
Jim does a runner out the back of the carpark and goes on the run.</span></span></span></span>

He flicked around channels, they all had the same tease, he didn’t want see it. 
Jim turned the TV off and threw the remote on the couch in disgust. He needed a shower to wash it all off.
Fifteen minutes later Jim had showered and changed, for the first time in what seemed forever, he felt comfortable. Time in the familiar safety of his own house, even besieged as it was by the media, had helped him to think more clearly.
Clean and comfortable he realised he was ravenous and headed for the kitchen to rummage up some food. 
He distracted himself from the weight of all his problems by making a gourmet sandwich, fresh toasted artisan bread, slathered with salted butter, some sliced real turkey and a perfectly ripe soft cheese. Normally he wouldn’t be so extravagant with all the fillings piled high, but this beautiful food, bought just a few days ago as a Level 8 VP at Nova Corp, was going to be his last luxury grocery shop for a long while, so there was absolutely no point waisting it.
He sat back down on the couch with his and thumbed on the TV. He didn’t want to see himself again so he browsed the sports channels to see if there was anything there that could take his mind of his situation. Just another reporter trying to get a scoop Jim thought as he pressed the reject button. He flipped through the phone and saw the same number had called 5 times already, one call after another almost immediately. 
Jim only had time to register this fact when the number called again, he needed to tell whoever it was to stop calling.
“Hello, who is this this? You need to stop calling” Jim said angrily.
The voice was distant and didn’t sound real ”You need to leave your house now”
“Who is this? look I’m not interested in anything you’ve got to offer”

“Turn on the news, you’ve got 15 minutes” The line went dead.

She paused listening to something in her ear. “I’m being told by my producers that the network will be pressing charges against Mr Dalton and we’re expecting his arrest imminently”
Jim, jumped up off the couch
NO! He coudn’t go to jail, that would be the end, there was no coming back from that.
Jim was panicking now, the voice on the other end of the phone had been right, he needed to leave, he couldn’t be arrested.
The adrenaline hit brain and the room blurred slightly as he fought to control himself.
Think! he yelled at himself, What did he need? in the back of his mind he knew once he’d left his house he was never coming back.
Money, he needed money. Jim bolted to his office at the front of the house.
Like the rest of the house it was a tastefully decorated prop, guests glancing in would see the dark wood desk sitting in front of custom built in bookcases decorated with books and souvenirs from thier travels and think just how well ready and travelled Jim and Sarah were. Of course it was all Sarahs’ work, Jim had little input when they furnished the office. 
He rushed to the desk and slammed open the top drawer so hard it came clean out of the desk and clattered to the floor it’s contents spilling over the ground. Jim flipped the drawer over and taped to the underside were two small grey items, they looked a lot like a memory sticks from the old days. 
Jim grabbed them and thanked his lucky stars Sarah hadn’t found them and also that he’d kept them all these years.
Jim had grown up in the Outer in a Level 5 household, so he learnt you always had a back-up plan. The sticks were the last inheritance of his parents, two untraceable caches of credits, the sum total of all thier assets in two tiny devices. He’d keep them out of sentimentality more than anything else.
He could see the blue and red flashing lights of the Metro Police bleeding around the edge of the curtains in his office, they must just have pulled up. 
He had to go.
His run to the back door was punctuated by trying to thrust on his runners at the same time. He stopped for a second out of habit looking for the remote to turn off the TV.
The footage of the TV sent a chill down his spine, the voiceover was breathless with anticipation “… as you can see here the Metro Police have arrived in numbers ready to take Jim Dalton into custody” the news coverage showed about a dozen Metro Police officers getting out of thier patrol cars and waving an armoured car through to Jim’s driveway “You can see here the Police are not taking any chances, they don’t know the extend of Daltons’ involvement in the Greys so they are taking every precaution. I’m also being told by a source that they are confident Dalton is still in the house…”
Jim looked at his phone laying next to the remote control, he turned on his heel slipped out his back door.
He immediately bolted to the fence he jumped over hours earlier and leap over into his neighbours backyard. Thankfully Elliot was back inside, the cabana was closed off an quiet, the backyard lights out, he did not want the one person who’d hadn’t shunned him today to get caught up in this.
Jim sprinted across the darkened yard and leapt over the fence to the Logans, the his next neighbour over. He dropped to the ground and he could hear the Police going around the side of his house one yard over, they weren’t trying to be quiet their radios updating thier movements.
He strained to hear what they were saying “Team two is at the rear door, no sign of the suspect, signs of life inside, lights and TV. Holding” a deep voice said in a clipped tone into a radio just loud enough to carry to Jim’s ears.
Jim sat his back against the fence catching his breath for a moment, he had to keep moving and put some distance between him and his house. With purpose he got up and started to more carefully climb over the next fence when a loud voice pierced the night. “Mr Dalton, this is the Metro Police, we have a warrant for your arrest, please come out peacefully”
Damn it! The lights went on in the yard he was just about to jump into, as did the lights in all the houses around him.
He Froze waiting for the light to come on where he was, then he remembered the Grants were away and the yard remained dark.
He was safe for a moment, but he was in a little oasis of darkness in a neighbourhood that was rapidly waking up.
The voice yelled again “Mr Dalton, this is the Metro Police, we have a warrant for your arrest, please come out peacefully, you have 5 minutes to comply” It had to be amplified by the armoured truck.

Then it hit him, the Grants were away and he knew how to get into thier house.</span></span></span></span>

 He stopped on one “.. as you can see by the footage here the Metro Police have now been joined by the Citizenship Enforcement Bureau as the operation here goes from arrest to investigation”

They followed the boy inside through the garage door and it smoothly closed behind them, eventually the lights in the garage went out and the front of the house fell silent.
Neil hadn’t considered that his family might not be there, they’d owned the house outright before he went into prison. His dreams of a reunion were dashed and he felt the weight being alone heavy on his shoulders as he turned around and deliberately walked away from his old life.

Neil responded in cautious tone “Morning Rook, it’s been a while since you’ve been on my bus”
 Rook nodded “I get around, as it happens I’ve got some work to do in your direction”
With that short exchange they both settled in for the trip the Rust Belt whilst the rest of the passengers took their seats and said thier Hello’s to friends and colleagues.
After a while Rook addressed Neil “ So Neil, how’s life on the outside treating you?”
Neil, nervous knew this was important “No as well as I would have hoped, in fact if I’m being honest pretty shitty actually”
Rook gave a short laugh “No.. it never lives up to the hype, more of the same out here as you have back inside”
Neil was pretty sure he was saying the right things, but he didn’t want to blow it said “Some days I don’t see the point, I can’t really see a way out”
Rook studies Neil for a few moments “It can feel like that, but you’ve only been out for a short time so let some time pass, mind your own business and you’ll find a way.”
He’d blown it, after weeks of waiting to find Rook, he laid it on too thick.
Deflated Neil mumbled “yep.. I expect you’re right, I’ve got all the time in the world now”
Rook nodded, apparently done with the conversation, looked out the window at the grey city sliding past. Neil just sat there staring at the back of the seat in front of him.
After a few minutes, without turning back to look at Neil, Rook said “Of course, you might just be feeling down because you don’t have any friends, did you consider that?”
Startled out of his funk, Neil looked at Rook, this was it “You’re right, I don’t have any friends out here, I think I’d like to start making some”
Rook turned to look at Neil, his eyes bore into Neil’s, but Neil didn’t shy away “Smartest thing you’ve said since I’ve met you Neil, perhaps there’s some hope for you yet” Rook smiled and broke his gaze with Neil.
The pressure of that stare was enough to unnerve Neil, but he needed to push forward. “So.. got any suggestions where I’d start?”
Rook shook his head and passed him a folded note “For when you get off the bus, make sure you shred it properly”
Not another word was spoken for the rest of the trip. Neil pondered the note, it was burning a hole in his pocket, he was desperate to know what was on it.
Finally, the bus arrived at his stop and Neil and most of the passengers got off. Rook didn’t move, just nodded his farewell.
Neil jumped off the bus and once he’d cleared the throng of workers at the bus stop he opened the note and read it: 
352 Langston Street 7pm, leave the phone in the apt.
It was hand written, Rook clearly had it ready for Jim, did he find Rook or did Rook find him Neil wondered.
He didn’t know the street, but he’d be able to look it up on one of the work terminals, he wasn’t going to miss this meeting, it might be his only change to get out of here.</span></span></span></span>

Rook nodded at the burly man who’d locked it shut, he turned away and walked down the corridor towards the front of the building and disappeared around a corner.
Neil stood there not knowing what to do, did he follow the man or not? 
Rook spoke in normal voice “Glad you could make it, sorry about the subterfuge, you never can be too careful, not everyone can keep their secrets” Rook’s eyes bore into Neil, was he waiting for him to say something? 
Neil didn’t flinch and shrugged “You do what you need to do I guess”
Rook simply nodded, the silence lingered. Neil avoided the need to fill it with hos own words, a trick he’d learnt in prison: silence was often a trap, baiting you into saying more than you wanted to. So he waited.

Rook, glancing back at Neil said coldly “Friends of yours maybe, you’d better hope there aren’t any”
Speaking again to the man “If any thing pop’s up you come running to us, understood?”
“Understood” said the man, and strode back down the corridor and out of sight.
Rook looked at Neil appraisingly “So, first test passed, but that was just the first course, the real test comes next” he gestured the down the corridor the opposite direction to the where man had gone and started walking.
Neil having been standing in the same spot for the last few minutes was caught flatfooted and he scrambled to catch up as Rook reached the end of the corridor, opened the door and waved Neil into the room.
Neil brushed past Rook and entered the room, it was hard to make out anything in the room, the LED ceiling panels were painted back just like in the corridor. He stepped inside the room a bit further instinctively to allow Rook to come in, but he didn’t. Rook simply smiled and closed the door behind Neil.
That was the second time the doors have been shut behind him tonight thought Neil as he stood in the dimly light room.
The room was silent and from what he could see empty, what the hell was this?
With a loud click, shocking bright lights flashed on directly in Neil’s face blinding him, instinctively he slammed his eyes shut as he put his hands up to shield his face from the painful brightness. He couldn’t see a thing, but he heard all to clearly a door open on the other side of the room and footstep clicking against the tiled floor.
“Hello Neil” a female voice said.
Who was this? Neil’s mind was racing, his eyes squeezed shut in pain making it hard to think.
“Take your time, relax you’ll get you eyesight back eventually” the female voice said.
He could hear furniture being dragged towards him, then the footsteps backed away. “There’s a chair on your right, take seat, you’ll be more comfortable”
Neil felt around and his hand hit the back of the chair, he slumped into the seat getting his bearing back “Can you turn off the fucking lights!”
“Sorry, can’t its part of the security protocol, it’s best for both of if you can’t identify me, they stay on.” she said in a matter of fact way.
Neil was rubbing his eyes, the bright spots were slowly fading and he risked cracking his eyelids open, the lights were still there, but had been turned down.
Squinting into the room he could make out a dark figure behind the lights, but that was all.
“Ok, I’m here and I’m blind, what did you want?” Neil asked getting annoyed now.
A chuckle “I like the fire in you’re belly, we could use that. I guess an introduction is in order, you can call me Vex” the voice was smooth and commanding.
Neil didn’t think Vex was someone he wanted to cross just form the way she spoke, he reminded himself he was in dangerous territory and to watch his words carefully.
Vex spoke again “My friend Rook tells me you’ve been having a bit of a tough time since you left prison?”
Neil answered “I won’t lie to you, it’s been shit, I may as well have stayed in prison for all the difference it makes”
“I believe that Neil, most of us know that we’ll never be amongst the elites, but Neil you’ve been there, a Level 7 no less, so you have a unique perspective” Vex said.
She continued “I also understand that you’ve had a warning for trying to reach your wife and Daughter?”
How did they know that? “Fuck their warning, who are they to tell me if I can or can;t see my own flash and blood” the subject still got Neil angry.
Vex calmly said “Neil, whilst I love the passion, a word of advice, keep it under wraps if you want to be my friend, I need people who can control themselves”
Chastened Neil responded “I can control myself just fine, but we’d better be talking about away to get the people who put me here”
“Oh Neil, we can do better than that. What if I told you your family never requested no contact, that they’ve been kept from you as much as you’ve been kept from them?” Vex’s voice was soothing.
Hope swelled up inside Neil, could this be true? were they just playing him?
Cautiously he said “I’d say that’s a big claim, you’d need to it prove to me”
“We can do that, lets make a deal, a quid pro quo if you will, I’ll get you in front of your family without any one knowing or being sent back to prison, if you’ll do something for me… how does that sound?” Vex asked.
Neil was floored, could they really do it? “what do I have to do?”
Vex, as smooth as ever said “We’ll let you know in due course, all I need to now is a yes or no”
Neil wasn’t sure what saying no would result in, but he didn’t have anything to loose anyway and said “You’ve got deal, but you’d better deliver”
“Back at you Neil, Rook will fill you in”
The light went out and the room was plunged into darkness as Neils eye’s had adjusted to the brightness. The door at the other end of the roon opened and closed as Vex left, Neil was alone again.
What had he agreed to do he wondered.</span></span></span></span>

Neil didn’t mind he wasn’t in much of a mood to have company anyway.

Neil was jolted away by the man sitting next to him elbowing him in the ribs, he had realising he’d fallen asleep. He glanced out of the window and saw they were only minutes from the bus stop at his office. The elbowing had stopped now the man saw Neil was awake. Before he could form any words to ask just what the hell he was doing, the man leaned in to Neil and said “Rook says hello”
Neil was instantly alert now, the mention of Rooks name dumped a jolt of adrenalin through his body dispelling any lingering grogginess. 
He asked the man “Are you a friend of Rooks?” 
The man nodded “You can call me Brask, Rook’s got a job for you, but he’s asked me to work with you on it”
Neil was a bit confused “I’ve got a job, and the deal I had with Vex was a two way street”
Brask looked around to make sure no one was listening in and gestured sharply to Neil to be quiet “Shhh… don’t say that name in public, not ever if you value your life. You’re lucky someone so important has taken an interest in you. From now on you deal only with me ok?” 
It was statement not a question, just like Rook did, Brask came looked fairly unremarkable, but there was a menace to the man that made Neil’s skin crawl.
Brask continued “I know about your deal, you do this one small job first and I’ll show you how you can see your family again” 
Neil wanting this conversation over “Ok, what is it”
Brask handed over a small flash card about the size of a thumbnail, with a handwritten note tightly wrapped around it and said “There’s a job Stratum Projects has worked on and we need to get all the plans for it, especially electrical, data and security. Dump it all on to the flash card, wear a red jumper to work when it’s done and someone will get the card from you. Names on the note, memorise it, destroy the note” Brask said completely flatly in a tone that said he wasn’t going to be repeating himself
Neil took the card and note “I’m not sure if I can access projects I’m not working on.” 
Brask bluntly said “Find a way, or no family reunion, you have three days”
The bus had just pulled up to the stop and Brask sprung to his feet and walked off, thier conversation was over. 
Neil pocketed the note wrapped flash card and took time to calm himself down, he was the last off the bus.
This was the point where he had to produce a result, Neil had made the decision a week ago to do whatever he needed to do see his family. but today it got real. He’d been expecting it, but he hadn’t anticipated the mixture of nerves and excitement at the task ahead.</span></span></span></span>

“Neil Lucas” one of them said gruffly.
Startled, Neil looked up to see them standing there staring at him expectantly.
“Yes” Neil stammered.
“Please come with us” They didn’t move just kept standing and staring.
Neil looking around could see all the other staff in the canteen also starting at him, he was sure his face was bright red, it certainly felt red hot.
“Now” prompted one of the guards.
Neil stood up and one guard motioned to Neil to follow the other guard and then fell into step behind Neil as he moved away from his half eaten lunch.
“Where are we going Neil ventured”
The guard behind him spoke “You been called to see the Director of security”
“Why?” Neil asked, he knew why.
“Apparently Mr Lucas you’ve been trying to access date outside your status level” said the guard walking behind Neil.
The guard in front clicked his tongue in disgust and said over his shoulder “You shouldn’t have told him that, that’s the Directors job, just keep you’re mouth shit ok”
“Relax, like I’ve said before, it’s not confidential if they’ve told us, beside what’s this guy going to do, run away now?”
“Just keep it shut from now on” the guard in front said as they entered a waiting  lift. The first guard turned away from them to press the floor button as Neil and the second guard followed inside, as they both turned the second guard discretely placed a finger on his grey uniform and tapped for just a moment.
It took Neil a second, but it quickly dawned on him that the guard had just given him a few precious minutes to come up with an excuse as to why he was running searched for Nova Corp. 
Minutes later Neil was marched into the 8th level office of the Security Director, as the name plate on the door told him. The Director was a small man with posture of someone who’d spent too much time in front of a terminal. He didn’t get up but instead addressed Neil immediately from behind his terminal screen.
“Neil, can I call you Neil” he asked.
“Sure” Neil answered, his heart still beating fast.
“Neil, I’ll get to the point, at 12:03pm you started searching for some data that was beyond your access level. According to the logs, you searched both on the company server and then the public database” he referred to his terminal screen “for a Nova Dynamics Corporation, is that correct?”
The few minutes he’d been given had allowed Neil to formulate a strategy here, tell the truth, or at least mostly the truth.
Neil answered “Yes, I did, I didn’t think searching for them was out of my access level until the system warned me”
The Director, satisfied with Neil’s answer said “Good, no point denying it, care to tell me why you were looking up this company?”
Neil opened his hands as a sign of compliance “I’ll be honest, Nova was one of the companies involved in my case, I guess I was just curious to see if they were still around”
“It sounds like you were digging into your old case” the director said “Neil, your case is old news, you were convicted and served a full sentence, there is nothing to gain from poking around in the past”
Neil didn’t say anything, the narrative he made up was working, better to keep quiet now.
Nodding as if Neil’s silence confirmed his suspicions, the Director continued “Ok Neil, you didn’t access any restricted data, but you did try, so we’ll be keeping an extra eye on you from now on. I’ll be putting a note on your file that we’ve had this discussion, but if I don’t need to talk to you again I’ll delete before your next review. If I do have to talk to you again it’s not going to be good for you, understand?”
“Yes” Neil said.
“My advice to you is to let your old case and any thoughts of digging around this Nova Corp die, you’ve got a chance a new life now, don’t waste it”
With that he waved at the two guards who had remained in the room for the whole conversation, as if Neil might have attacked the Director “Take him back please”
Neil walked away relieved, but he’d have to be much more careful now, that was too close.</span></span></span></span>

Brask sat next to Neil’s now customary empty seat and let out a few big breaths trying to slow his breathing down. Brask’s grip didn’t loosen “I’m on the hook just as much as you are, if you don’t deliver, then I don’t deliver and I’m not looking to get sanctioned” with that statement Brask let go of Neil’s arm.
The intense stare remained “Now tell me how you’re going to get the files.”
It was all or nothing now and he didn’t like the sound of being sanctioned either, Neil said “I tried once and almost got caught, I can’t get the files you want from my terminal, they’re well above me grade as a Level 3. Just typing in the project number got me pinged”
Brask had calmed down slightly and asked “You didn’t waste my time this morning to tell me how you can’t do it, you must have an idea have how you can do it?”
Neil answered “Yes, that’s why I needed to talk to you, I know how to get the files, but I need help.” He paused “is it safe to talk here?”
Brask, patted the pocket where the little grey device was and said “We’re good to talk, nothing will overhear us”
Ok, so not recording, but blocking thought Neil, he’d have to trust Brask on that, he outlaid his plan “There’s a Level 6 on the floor who manages the whole office, not me personally, but he manages the level 5’s who manage us.  Neil ploughed on “I thought I saw a sign from one of the security guards who saved my arse yesterday, maybe he is sympathetic to us? Maybe he’s someone who could help with the camera’s in the office?” 
That was it, Neil’s plan as much it it was, if he couldn’t solve the security camera issues he didn’t have a back up.
Brask looked at Neil, not saying anything just pondering what Neil has just said.
Eventually he spoke “I don’t know anything about any security guards. What I do know is your plan is pretty damn flimsy” 
Brask was silent again, so was Neil, his plan looked like it had failed before it had even started.
Brask nodded and finally said “Ok, I’ll see what I can do. Don’t do anything today, I’ll be in touch”
Brask made a show of reaching into his pocket and switching off the blocker, then putting his head back and closing his eyes. Now he had to work out how to hack into his bosses terminal.</span></span></span></span>

It was not a complicated task and it would be done in minutes, he might even get some time for lunch afterwards.
After an eternity his terminal chimed for the lunch break, the staff on the floor made thier way out of the office to the canteen. No one gave Neil a second looked when he didn’t get and go with the crowd, no asked him to join them, seems they were all happy for him to stay in the office, Neil felt invisible.
Neil had seen manager leave his office at least fifteen minutes before the lunch break, being a Level 6 out here in the Rust Belt meant being the top of the heap, so there were no timed lunches for him, he could come and go as he pleased.
That was it, the last group had left the office, Neil waited until the lift doors closed on them. “Go Now!” the told himself as started to hesitate.
He stood abruptly up from his desk and walked briskly across the large open plan office, past the now empty desks and terminals, past the little bank of  waist height bookshelves and cupboards that created a corridor between and the main worked and and the glass offices. 
Neil looked the the camera on the ceiling as he walked into the manager’s office, there was no indication if it was working or now, he was taking a leap of faith that no one was watching on the other end.
Neil skirted around the desk and sat at the terminal, it was locked. He knew it would be, most terminals were opened automatically by the authorised users smartphone or watched, so no one used password anymore. Neil, being a Level 3, didn’t get the luxury of smart wearables and had to log in to his terminal manually. The systems tech who showed him how to log-in on his first day, told him it was little hack they’d built just for him as he was the only Level 3 they’d ever had in the office.
Neil just hoped the same hack worked on this terminal.
He keyed in the sequence to open up the manual log-in. Yes! the script worked and the manual log-in prompt appeared. 
Neil typed in the manager’s name, Brentan Hall, in the same format as he typed in his own. 
He typed in the system password he remebered the tech use to activate his terminal back on that first day, he hadn’t meant to look, but the tech took no care to hide it, Neil just hoped it was a universal password.
[User name and password don’t match]
Damn it, did he remember it correctly? Neil very deliberately typed the password again making sure he didn’t make any mistakes.
[User name and password don’t match]
Neil wasn’t sure how many attempts he had, or if he could actually get in at all now. He was starting to sweat with the prospect of failure.
The office was quiet apart from the low hum of the air-conditioning, otherwise Neil wouldn’t have heard the lift quietly chime as it’s doors opened. Brentan Hall stepped out. Shit! 
He quickly exited the log-in prompt and looked up, Brentan was already half way to the office and moving fast. Neil didn’t have time to leave without being seen and had no choice but to duck into the small ensuite attached to the office, he slide the door close just as Brentan stepped in.
He was talking on his phone “Yep, I’m in my office now, give me two minutes, the boss is riding me to get this report sent” He sat at the desk and clicked through his emails looking for something.
“Don’t you leave without me you arseholes! Remember who’s paying for the first round!” He said all to loudly in the empty office, Neil only meters away in the ensuite held his breath.
“Here it is, these fucking criminals I have to babysit finally did something right… and it’s sent, no need to come back here today! I’ll be back down there in sixty seconds”
Neil could hear Brentan exit the office just as loudly and quickly as he entered, after a few second he snuck the ensuite door open and saw Brentan entering the lift, still on his phone.
Neil looked back into the office, Brentan hadn’t logged off his terminal, he’s just walked out assuming, as most people would, the terminal would automatically log-him off in a minute or two.
What a stroke of luck, Neil rushed to the terminal to stop it from shutting down. His heart was racing at the near miss, but the terminal was open with full access, he quickly opened up the file database and entered in the project number.
This time the search came back with the full project listing and no warnings.
[Project 243/402/143 – Nova Dynamics Corporation – Datacentre]
[Open project folder? Y/N]
Neil opened the folder, inside were multiple subsidiary folders, jackpot!
He placed the flash card on the screen and dragged all of the files over it to copy them across. Neil checked the clock on the terminal, it had been almost twenty minutes since lunch was called, he need to get out of this office.
Done! All files successfully copied, Neil pocket the card and logged out of the database and bolted out of the office. He didn’t go back to his desk but over to the bathroom, he need to wash the sheen of sweat of his face and take some big deep breaths.
Ten minutes later Neil was sitting comfortably back at his desk when the first of his colleagues started trickling back from lunch. Just as they had when they left, they ignored Neil who looked like he just been siting there working the whole time.

He was glad to see Grant’s office was empty, this was a huge step outside the rules and he didn’t think Grant was the kind of person who was going to looked past it.
Neil went out through the rec room and the laundry to the back exit where the rubbish was kept. 
There was a nondescript white EV waiting, it was nothing fancy and certainly didn’t look out of place out here in the Outer. Neil approached the car and the passenger side door opened, he tried to see who was in the car before he got in, but the tinting had been turn up to full.
Neil hesitantly got into the car, he was greeted by a dark haired woman sitting behind the wheel.
“Hi Neil, big day for you” she said.
Neil recognised that voice, but not the face, last time they spoke all he could see was as black silhouette as bright lights had blinded him.
“Vex” Neil ventured.
“At your service, now please close the door so we can get going” Vex said as Neil realised he’d been sitting there with the door open, perhaps subconsciously leaving an escape exit if he needed it.
He closed the door, a bit shocked Vex was the driver today, he’d expected another menacing Grey to do the job. 
Vex drove off and didn’t say anything. Neil saw the car’s console was black, no graphics, no controls, just completely blank with one flashing word in the top right hand corner: [operating]. 
Vex saw what he was looking at and gestured to the screen with one had, the other remained on the steering wheel and said “We’re pretty proud of that, it took quite some time and effort to develop that, we almost had to rebuild the car to get it to work though and of course it’s manual drive only now”
Neil realised that Vex had actually been driving the whole time, for someone who was used to auto driving for most of this life, he wasn’t all that comfortable at the thought of a person manually driving.
Vex could see Neil’s discomfort and laughed “Don’t worry, I’m actually a pretty good driver, I thought I could do with the practice today.”
Neil was once again in a situation he didn’t expect, but he was starting to get the idea that was their aim. Trying to be as nonchalant as he could be about Vex driving the car, he asked “Where are we going?”
“Not far actually, your daughter has an appointment with her doctor…”
Neil immediately interrupted “What? What’s wrong?”
“Don’t worry nothing’s wrong, it’s just a routine check up, she’s healthy and your wife’s healthy” said Vex not looking at Neil, but concentrating on the road.
Good, thought Neil, but this was still very odd and he couldn’t quite make sense of it “So I’m seeing them after the appointment?”
“No, you’ll be meeting them in the Doctor’s office. Neil officially they don’t want to see you, so we had to find a way to get you together without any eyeballs or cameras spotting you, after all right now you’re in bed sick” Vex said.
“They will want to see me, I know my family better than anyone” Neil said.
Vex simply said “We don’t know if that’s true or not, we couldn’t find any evidence they’ve tried to reach you in all these years, even after you got released, either way you’ll know the answer soon enough”
Neil was always so confident that his wife wouldn’t have abandoned him, he was always so sure there was good reason he hadn’t heard from her in all this time. He’d stuck to the though that perhaps she;’d tired but had been prevented from doing so. Vex’s snippet of information cut him deeply, what if it was true, that she really wanted nothing to do with him? The thought was too hard to bear.
“Do they even know I’m coming?” asked Neil.
Vex paused before she answered “No, they don’t know, best we could do is find this appointment in her schedule and change the doctor to a more sympathetic friend of ours.”
Neil didn’t actually care about the details og how they’d done it, he just wanted to get there and prove that he was right, he sat silently in the car trying not to let the doubts take over.
After a few minutes of silence, Vex spoke “So, that data you got for us, nice job. It’s going help us a hell of lot. I think you might have a future with us actually”
Neil wasn’t particularly interested in that conversation right now. “Ok, sure, lets just get me to my family and we can talk later”
They had driven from his halfway house right in the middle of the Outer through to the loose transition into the Green. Vex pulled into the underground carpark of a large public medical centre and parked in a spot well away from the lift. The lights in this section weren’t working creating a dark oasis within the brightly light carpark.
Vex turned to Neil, no more of the chatty demeanour, she was deadly serious, her eyes cold and dark “You have fifteen minutes, not a minute more. If you’re one second late I’m leaving, get your own way home, understood?”
Neil nodded, he didn’t have his phone, his cards, or any way to get back to his apartment, so being late was going to be an option.
Vex pointed the to the opposite side of the carpark from the public lift “Over there, see the service life, you take that one, there’s a nurse waiting for you and she’ll take you where you need to go. Time starts now.”</span></span></span></span>

 The man spoke again “If you’re wondering who I am, you can call me Rook, I might be able to help you get out of the bind you’re in.”

Rook didn’t answer instead he said “Take the next exit please.”

Jim pulled over, Rook immediately pulled out a what looked like a battery about the size of an old brick, Jim didn’t see him bring that in the car, he must have got it in the van when they stopped to speak to Vex. Without asking Jim to move, Rook leaned over the centre console and started fumbling around with the plug end of a lead attached to the battery. Jim moved his legs out of the way and said “Whoa, what are you doing, what is that?”
Rook was looking for something under the console “There’s a diagnostics port somewhere under the steering wheel, I need to plug this into… dont just site there it’s easier for you to do it”
“What are we doing?” Jim asked.
“We’re leaving the car here, but we need to clean this system first, this will wipe the memory” said Rook.
Jim understood, and he felt around under the steering wheel and almost immediately found it “Here it is” he said to Rook who passed him the plug.
Once it was plugged Rook pressed the only switch on the box, the centre console and the dash immediately stuttered and went blank, a faint smell of burning plastic and electronics started to seep into the cabin.
“What did you do?”Jim asked
“Nothing wipe a system like a massive burst of electricity, this little booster will fry just about any circuit” said rook as reached the steering wheel and unplugged the cable.
The smell of burning was growing stronger by the second, Jim was looked across at Rook, who raised his eyebrows at the tendrils of smoke now starting to seep out from under the dashboard. “Of course too much juice and you can set off a chain reaction, we might want to get out. Now”
Jim didn’t need to be asked twice as both of them jumped out of the car that was rapidly filling with smoke. 
The black van that was parked in the basement garage pulled up next to Jim and Rook, the side door shooting open before it had stopped. Rook jumped in without hesitation, Jim paused which elicited a rebuke from Rook “Fucking get in, we have to go!”
Jim jumped in and before his feet even hit the floor of the van, it was darting forward making him stumble backwards into Rook, there was no sign of Vex. He straightened up and looked back out through the rear window as the van sped off, he could see flames curling up the side of the Grant’s car from the battery pack underneath. Very soon it would be engulfed in flame, a fire that like all battery fires couldn’t be put out. He felt a bit guilty seeing the car burning like, he knew the Grant’s well and he was genuinely sorry for firstly stealing the car and then getting it destroyed like that. 
Rook was watching it burn just like Jim until they turned around a corner and lost sight of it forever. He had a satisfied smile on his face, looking at him Jim suddenly knew burning the car to the ground was the result Rook wanted, the thought didn’t fill Jim with much comfort, had he just made his situation worse?.</span></span></span></span>

“If you’re worried about being close to the Scar, don’t be, the deadly fog stories are old wives tales, at worst it smells for a day or two, but being in here keeps most of the small out.”

Rook continued “I’m not staying, I’ve got places to be, someone will be along soon enough, there’s supplies in the kitchen, the bathroom is downstairs and whatever you do, do not leave this building.”

He looked to the kitchenette all the way at the other end of the room, there was nothing cooking there was no sign of Corra. Jim got up, being careful to avoid making any noise he walked to the top of the stairs that went down to the ground floor. He was causally looking around the room as if he was trying to find his way in an unfamiliar house, but in reality he was just looking for cameras. He couldn see any obvious ones though. He stopped and listened intently at the top of the stairs, he didn’t hear any sounds coming up from downstairs and as stealthily as he could he descended.
Downstairs all the walls seemed to be intact, the bottom of the staircase led into a small hallway dimly lit by sunlight bleeding in around the edges of the window on what Jim assumed was the back door. The windows downstairs hadn’t been bricked up, merely painted over. Jim snuck over to the door and tried the handle, it was locked, it couldn’t be that easy could it thought Jim.
He saw the bathroom door was open just a few steps away and he went inside to avoid being seen trying to open the door.

Now let’s grab some breakfast upstairs there’s some people coming in soon to work on your next move” she motioned for Jim to go back up the stairway.
This was the moment thought Jim, more people were coming and he might not get the chance again. He stepped aside as if going around Corra to go up the stairs, crucially it put her in between him and the open door to the bathroom. She was caught totally unprepared for the shove and barrelled into the bathroom without any control smashing into the wall at the back of the room and falling heavily on the tile floor.
Jim slammed the door shut behind her, he deliberately stood back and kicked the door handle, his foot bounced off. He lined up another kick and the handle snapped off the door with a satisfying crack. He grabbed the spindle that was exposed and pulled it out so Corra couldn’t open the door.
Corra was banging on the door now yelling at Jim “Let me out, Jim don’t do this!”
Jim turned his attention to the door with his adrenalin pumping he launched a two footed kick to the door to get it open. It was stronger than he’d anticipated and he just bounced off. Jumping straight up he kicked at the door, once, twice and a third time, still the door didn’t budge.

Jim didn’t answer, Corra resumed kicking the door, the frame cracked as Corra, it would only be a few more kicks and she’s be out. Jim had to move now.
He pushed the biggest of the broke shards of glass out of the frame and climbed through to the small backyard. He clambered over the side fence as he heard the door inside burst open.
Jim didn’t know where he was going, but he hurled him self over three more side fences until he came landed in a laneway. He sprinted into the street and turned away from the townhouse not looking back to see if he was being followed, just wanting to put distance between him and the safe house.
He saw another lane way and ducked into it, Jim was panting hard now as the adrenalin emptied out of his system. He needed a place to recover, the laneway went all the way across to another street, he sprinted for it and quickly turned the corner. This street was a bit different, the town houses it empty shops. He couldn’t run anymore, his legs were like lead and he was seeing little stars in the corner of his eyes. He saw the boards on one of the shops was loose so he squeezed his was in behind it inside, pulling it close after him. 
The inside of the shop was just an empty space, the only furnishing was the dust on the floor. His legs totally spent, Jim slid down against the wall in a heap, laying on the dusty floor listening for any sing of pursuit. 
After a moment, he shifted slightly a sharp pain stabbed in his leg and he looked down to see his pants red with blood. Gingerly he examined himself, there was a slash in pants was oozing out blood. He must have cut himself climbing through the window. Jim ripped the cut in his pants open to see just how badly he was cut, it wasn’t too deep and had started to close up already, but lying on the ground as he was it certainly wasn’t clean. 
He slowly got up to explore the shop and see if he could get some water to clean the cut up a bit, the sound of a car stopped him dead. This area was abandoned so the only car the could be out there was the Grey’s looking for him. It drove past without stopping and Jim took in a deep breath.
He’d have to patient and methodical to get out the area, but he was now even more determined to get back to territory he was familiar with, that would give him at least an even chance of survival. That meant getting back into the heart of the Outer where he grew up and disappearing into the crowd.</span></span></span></span>

He stepped aside as if going around Corra to go up the stairs, crucially it put her in between him and the open door to the bathroom. Jim stepped next to Corra and shoved her, as hard as he could into the bathroom. She was caught totally unprepared for the shove and barrelled into the bathroom without any control smashing into the wall at the back of the room and falling heavily on the tile floor.
Jim slammed the door shut behind her, he deliberately stood back and kicked the door handle, his foot bounced off. He lined up another kick and the handle snapped off the door with a satisfying crack. He grabbed the spindle that was exposed and pulled it out so Corra couldn’t open the door.
Corra was banging on the door now yelling at Jim “Let me out, Jim don’t do this!”
Jim turned his attention to the door with his adrenalin pumping he launched a two footed kick to the door to get it open. It was stronger than he’d anticipated and he just bounced off. Jumping straight up he kicked at the door, once, twice and a third time, still the door didn’t budge.
Corra was doing the same, the banging on the bathroom door was now a rhythmic beat as she tired to kick the door open from the inside. Jim could she she’d beat him to the punch, he needed another option. He looked around and saw the broken door handle on the floor, quickly he picked it up and threw it as hard as he could into the window into the door. The glass shattered, the gaping hole let the early morning sunlight stream in.
The smashing of the glass stopped Corra’s kicking, she yelled from the other side of the door to Jim “Jim, think about what you’re doing, if you leave you’ll be on your own, we won;t take you back, Vex will hunt you down, Jim, are you there?”
Jim didn’t answer, Corra resumed kicking the door, the frame cracked as Corra, it would only be a few more kicks and she’s be out. Jim had to move now.
He pushed the biggest of the broke shards of glass out of the frame and climbed through to the small backyard. He clambered over the side fence as he heard the door inside burst open.
Jim didn’t know where he was going, but he hurled him self over three more side fences until he came landed in a laneway. He sprinted into the street and turned away from the townhouse not looking back to see if he was being followed, just wanting to put distance between him and the safe house.
He saw another lane way and ducked into it, Jim was panting hard now as the adrenalin emptied out of his system. He needed a place to recover, the laneway went all the way across to another street, he sprinted for it and quickly turned the corner. This street was a bit different, the town houses it empty shops. He couldn’t run anymore, his legs were like lead and he was seeing little stars in the corner of his eyes. He saw the boards on one of the shops was loose so he squeezed his was in behind it inside, pulling it close after him. 
The inside of the shop was just an empty space, the only furnishing was the dust on the floor. His legs totally spent, Jim slid down against the wall in a heap, laying on the dusty floor listening for any sing of pursuit. 
After a moment, he shifted slightly a sharp pain stabbed in his leg and he looked down to see his pants red with blood. Gingerly he examined himself, there was a slash in pants was oozing out blood. He must have cut himself climbing through the window. Jim ripped the cut in his pants open to see just how badly he was cut, it wasn’t too deep and had started to close up already, but lying on the ground as he was it certainly wasn’t clean. 
He slowly got up to explore the shop and see if he could get some water to clean the cut up a bit, the sound of a car stopped him dead. This area was abandoned so the only car the could be out there was the Grey’s looking for him. It drove past without stopping and Jim took in a deep breath.
He’d have to patient and methodical to get out the area, but he was now even more determined to get back to territory he was familiar with, that would give him at least an even chance of survival. That meant getting back into the heart of the Outer where he grew up and disappearing into the crowd.</span></span></span></span>

The clerk looked at the stick, he knew what it was and Jim could see the greed spark in his eyes. 
 “If that’s what I think it is I might have something for you, wait here” He left the counter and went out the back, Jim waited for either the clerk to come back of sirens from the metro police turning up to arrest him.
It was the clerk who came back, hold a pair of black pants, they were clearly store uniform. “I’ve got these, they should fit you, going to cost you 500 credits.”
500 credits thought Jim, they should only cost 50 credits or so. “500? Come on man, that’s steep.”

Jim didn’t really have a choice. “Throw the cap in and we’re good.”

“Want a balance?” He asked.
No fucking way thought Jim, you’re not finding out how much I’ve got on there, he simply said. “All good man, It’s probably tapped out after that. Got a place to change”
The clerk pointed over to the office door without saying a word. Jim went in and changed as quickly as he could, he had the feeling the clerk wanted more of his credits, perhaps the whole stick in fact. He donned the new cap and left the store walking away briskly so the Clerk would get any ideas.
Jim walked the streets deeper into the heart of the Outer and felt safer, he was less conspicuous and in familiar territory, it hadn’t really change in the past twenty or so years since he left. For the first time since Nova Corp had released the footage from the Apex restaurant, Jim was in control.</span></span></span></span>

She continued “In breaking new just released today, the Metro Police tell me they discovered a very high tech chip modification on Mr Dalton‘s TV in his house, one that allowed access to citizenship restricted material.”
Shane involuntarily uttered the word “Shit” under his breath.
The News story went on, Lina the anchor now asking questions “That’s a very interesting development indeed Kira, what do you think that means?”
“Lina when you add up how Mr Dalton was able to escape arrest by highly trained officers from both the Metro Police and the CEB, the fact he was able to set off the cell overload and now the revelation that he had highly sophisticated contraband chips in his TV at home, it paints a worrying picture of a dangerous and well connected person.”
“It certainly does, are the Police any closer to finding Mr Dalton?”
“No Lina, they are telling me privately that Mr Dalton has completed disappeared, however they are getting leads form citizen fro all over the city claiming to have seen him, some even from as far out as the Scar’s fog zone, they tell me there are methodically checking each lead and are confident they track Mr Dalton down quickly”
“We all hope, I know we’ll feel better once he’s safe and in custody” said Lina.
Shane tapped the keyboard to mute the sound, he sat silently contemplating the the update about Jim.
There was a knock on the office door, Jim looked up to see Rob Hughes standing in the doorway. “Hi sire, I’m, here for our 10am project briefing.”
“Yes, come in, good timing Rob. First lets grab some coffee” Shane said as he gesture the the antique sideboard loaded with fresh fruit, pastries and a beautifully ornate copped coffee machine.</span></span></span></span>

Robb nodded “Yes Sir, we still don’t know how they got hold of the data to block our moves, but we’re working on it.”
“You probably won’t find it, Pinnacle is better at data hacking than anyone, but keep trying to see where we leaked though, would be good to plug the hole.” said Shane.
“Next project is number 23, as you recommended we’ve burned the project, the subject and associates have been terminated and all records expunged.” 
Shane nodded, “Good, I know it’s distasteful, but it was necessary. I want a review on all the testing we have for the subject and a reason why it went off the rails so badly by at our next meeting.”
Rob paled slightly and said “Yes sir” he picked up the file he’d placed on the coffee table at the start of the meeting “Now we get to project 29 Sir, lots of news on that one”
Shane sat forward and looked intently as Rob “Yes, I saw the latest bulletin, please explain how we’ve fucking lost him?”
Rob fumbled with the file momentarily, but quickly regained his composure “Sir, you’re correct that we did loose him, but it was for less than 48 hours, however he’s back in our sights now. I received and update just before I came in here that one of our scouts out near the Scar saw him and was able to get a tracker on him.”
Shane smiled slightly “That’s good news, get in contact with him and push the project forward as planned”
“Yes sir, already in motion”
Shane asked “Can we account for the missing 48 hours?”
“No Sir we can’t, we believe the Greys took him off the streets and moved him around until just recently.”
“Ok, there’s some work to here, we need to find out where he went and what he did with these Greys, it’s just not acceptable to have a subject missing for the best part of two days. Also I want to get us inside the Greys, the fact they are invisible to us is worrying. I need to know if any of the other Board companies are behind them.”
Shane stood up signalling an end to the meeting, Rob followed suit not missing the hint and retrieved all the files. They both walked over to the office door where Shane placed a hand on his shoulder in what anyone watching would have seen as a friendly gesture. He leaned in and said calmly and quietly, his hand still resting lightly on Rob’s shoulder “Rob, this project is feeling a lot like Project 23, I don’t want two projects crashing and burning so close to each other. Get control of this one or your position as Director of Special Projects might come to and end too, I don’t want to have to burn you along with it” He smile was warm and genuine despite the cold threat.
With that Shane patted Rob’s shoulder and gestured for him to leave, the meeting was over , Rob knew he was on borrowed time if he didn’t deliver.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">section 4 of chapter 15: In the hours that passed Rob had stayed in his office waiting for updates from his team. Getting the Dalton project back on track was quite literally the most important task he’d ever had, he needed laser focus to turn his fortunes around. 
His team on the ground were professionals and as instructed started dropping secured updates each hour, so far there was nothing of consequence, but Rob expected it would take some time to ramp up thier activity. 
In the meantime he needed to go back through all the data points to see what they’d missed about this subject Jim Dalton and how he was the second subject to get away from him in short order.
Nova Corp, through it’s various subsidiaries cast a wide net all the way from elementary and high school through to college and corporate testing to find candidates with the right mix of intelligence, independence, and resilience for thier special projects. Each time a citizen did any kind of test, Nova Corp scooped up the data, analysed it and used it for thier gain. At any one time they had a database of likely candidate for all kinds of jobs, actions and special projects.
Rob was looking through the raw data from Jim Dalton’s files to see if the appraisals team had made any errors or missed something. There was a knock at the door, it was Grace his executive assistant, she looked worried, had she picked up on the precarious position Rob was in? He wasn’t in the mood to discuss it one way or thew other?
“Grace, I don’t want to be disturbed today please” he told her.
“I know, Mr Hughes, but this is really important, I’ve just sent you a link to a video you need to watch” she said.
“I don;t have time for video’s today Grace, I’ll look at it later”
“Sorry Mr Hughes but it’s from Mr Dalton, it’s all over the news” 
Rob’s blood ran cold at the mention of Dalton, what new fuck-up had dropped in his lap from this project? He clicked on the link from Grace, it was from a well known gossip site, not the news. The sensational video title was “Dalton proclaims his innocence from unknown location”
Rob looked up and Grace was still standing there “Out” he yelled. He clicked the play button without bothering to see if Grace left or not.
The video opened on Jim sitting in a run down hotel room, the backdrop of peeling wall paint and the dim light making it look like Jim was back in a jail, he spoke.
“Hello, my name is Jim Dalton and… well I’m not sure what I want to say here… umm, first of all I’m not who the news makes me out to be, I’m no master criminal or anything like that. Sure I’m guilty of getting drunk and being rude to staff, which I know was wrong” the video must have been shot on a phone, for a second it went black as Jim inadvertently put his hand over the lense. 
The image cam back and Jim continued “Is that enough to ruin someones life over? I worked my way up from the Outer to Level 8 just like they say you can, but one mistake and it’s all gone. One bad day and the press are at your doorstep and the Police and the CEB are coming to arrest you. Is that fair?”
Jim looked around as if there was a sound off screen, not hearing anything further he spoke again “I’m not going to jail for something like that, did anyone ever ask who else was at lunch? Who invited me there and paid for all the wine? Who leaked the footage to the media? No the media just made me out to be some villain, just like you’ve seen before, I’m not, were they? I’m just a normal working man who is being made an example of so none of you ever step out line… to the media who hounded me out of my house, do your job a dig deeper.” The video went to black and ended.
Rob sat at his desk processing what he’d just seen, after a moment he yelled into the empty office “Fuck! Fuck! This fucking arsehole is going to get me killed” he slammed his hands down onto the desk so hard he felt pain shoot up his arms. This was the worst possible thing that could have happened. He needed to take stock.
The phone rang, it wasn’t routed through Grace’s desk as per normal, this was coming in direct, only one person could do that, Shane.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Last part of chpater 15: Rob broke out in a cold sweat, he couldn’t take the call, he just didn’t have an answer for Shane and he needed one desperately. Instead he almost bolted out of the office, as he rushed past Grace sitting at her desk and said “Tell him I’m in the bathroom”, Grace didn’t get the chance to answer as Rob was already gone.
He’d made his way to the executive bathroom, luckily it was empty, breathing a sight of relief he pulled out a mobile from his pocket and punched in a number, it was answered immediately “John, have you seen Dalton’s video?”
John without emotion “Yes Sir”
“And… any thoughts o how to play this?” Rob asked.
“It seems to me this could align well with our goals for the project, even speed up the timeline”
“Explain”
“Once I make contact, I’ll encourage more video’s, but I’ll steer him towards our goals and minimise any damage to us. We can build up a strong narrative to damage our competitors if we drop the right information into Dalton’s lap and encourage more videos”.
Rob was quiet and thought it over. Yes it could work, he’d never have thought of Dalton going public himself, he’d always planned for the media to do the work of using Dalton’s story to undermine the other Board Companies, but this could be much more powerful.
“Ok, do it, how close are you to making contact?” 
“Give me twenty-four hours, I’ve got a lead that I’m chasing down now”
“Ok keep me updated” Rob said and cut the line.
He looked at himself in the mirror, smoothed down his suit jacket and adjusted his tie, he was back in control, look like it he told himself.
Rob sauntered back to his office as if he didn’t have a worry in the world, he breezed past Grace without a word. He immediately dialled Shane’s direct number from his desk phone, Shane picked up in two rings, he didn’t speak.
Rob jumped straight in “Sorry Sir, I just stepped out of the office for a quick break, did you want an update?”
“Yes Rob, I want an update as to why Jim Dalton is now releasing videos onto the net?”
“That’s part of the project plan, I felt it would speed up our goals and be more authentic if Dalton was used directly instead of through media proxies” that was a stretch, but he’d put it out there now.
Silence for a moment, then “Rob, remind me again what the project goals are please?”
He wasn’t buying it though Rob, he needed to be careful this was a tightrope ”This was a phase one project, creating a sympathetic public figure and sow discord about the system.”
“And why are we doing that?”
Rob swallowed “I must admit Sir, I don’t have access to the full project goals, but I’m assuming we want to leverage this public pressure against one or more of the Board companies to our advantage.” He hoped he was correct.
“That’s sounds about right Rob, but bear in mind you don’t know what the end game is here, so before you go off on your own again, do me a favour and run it by me, ok?”
“Yes Sir.”
“This is a novel play with the videos, play it out for now, but know this, my finger is hovering over the burn button, so don’t let it get out of hand.” the line was disconnected.
Rob slumped back into his chair, he’d gone way out on a limb there, but it seemed to have worked. He now had some time to unscrew this mess, he buzzed Grace “Grace, can you get me our media director in here, tell him to cancel his plans for the day we’ve got some work to do.”</span></span></span></span>

They called it the Reach and it wasn’t a place you went to unless you were desperate or degenerate. The Reach was a sprawling district on the far side of the Outer from the Scar, where the city butted up against the as yet unsettled mountains. It was a place where you could buy pretty much anything if you had the credits. The Metro Police mostly left it alone as long as the area as a whole stayed quiet and out of the news. It was a mixing pot of all levels, from those who had nowhere else to go, to the upper levels looking for some illicit thrills away from prying eyes.
It took the rest of the credits on one of his sticks to get a black market burner phone, the seller guaranteed it was untraceable, but Jim wasn’t taking any chances  and the phone remained powered off until he needed it again.
He knew it was a desperate move to upload the video, Jim reasoned that there was enough interest in his story the news might pick it up and just maybe his side of the story would get out there. So far nothing had hit the news yet.
He lay still on the bed, barely moving, physically and mentally exhausted, the weight of his current situation pressing him further into the sagging mattress.
 His last hope, the Greys turned out to be just another group of people who wanted to use him for thier own ends, he was done with that, from now on he resolved he’d only deal on his own terms. If he crashed and burned, he’d make them all hurt on the way down.
The flashing red alert banner on the TV caught Jim’s attention and roused him out of his dozing. He sat up and listened intently, the anchor was clearly excited at this news “We have a breaking news story, former Level 8 executive and wanted fugitive Jim Dalton has uploaded a video proclaiming his innocence from charges of assault, criminal damage, theft and arson from his three day crime spree and also denying any connection to dissident group the Greys. We’ll have a deep dive into the video and Dalton’s claims at the top of the hour, be sure to join us then” the channel moved back to it’s current show.
Jim lay back on the bed pleased his gamble had paid off, perhaps the tide of public opinion was going to turn for him. Looking at the clock on the TV he had about twenty minutes, plenty of time to get some supplies before it would be too hard to walk around in public safely.</span></span></span></span>

John had access to Dalton’s whole life story from Nova, he knew how he thought, how he’d react under pressure, how far he’d go to save himself, or so he’d thought. Dalton had surprised them all with the video, that kind of resourcefulness wasn’t in the files. John knew full well the files weren’t everything, under intense pressure people could do unexpected things, the could learn and adapt. If his boss ever got out into the field and did the kind of work John did for him, he might have understood this.
Not that he didn’t respect Rob Hughes, any Level 8 who had the ear of the CEO of one of the Board companies was a full measure of respect, but they lived a life disconnected from the people out here in the Outer. Even if the did sneak into the Reach for some debauchery, people like John were always waiting in the shadows to save them from themselves.
He’d worked on the Dalton project from it’s very beginning and had built up a begrudging respect for the man, they put him though hell and he hadn’t crumbled yet. Still that wouldn’t stop Rob from using Dalton as a pawn to displace Rob and take his seat, a seat he knew he do a better job sitting in.
His phone rang, he clicked the earpiece and said “Speak to me”, after a few seconds he nodded and ended the call.
He took a sip of his coffee and grimaced, it wasn’t very good, there was no real coffee out here just a cheap synthetic brew that sort of approximated coffee, sometimes. He flicked through his contacts on his phone and dialled Rob.
Rob must have been waiting with his phone in his hand as he answered halfway through the first ring “Have you got news John?” he demanded.
John answered calmly “Yes Sir, one of my spotters tell me he’s holed up in a hotel in the Reach, I’m not far from there, I should have eyes on soon”
“Good work John, what’s the play when you make contact?”
“Right now I’m not sure, I’ll need some time to see where his head is at before I make a move, first contact is always a fluid situation, I can’t sell him straight away.” said John, he never prejudged how a first contact went, people had strong bullshit meter and if you were pushing an agenda you’d get found out most of the time.
“Ok, understand this, we don’t have a lot of time here, the video is going mainstream and we need to get in front on this now” Rob was getting agitated again.
John answered simply “Understood Sir, I’ll update once contact is made” and killed the call. 
He sat at the rickety table and looked at the now cold fake coffee in front of him, Rob was going to be a problem he thought. 
He got up and left the cafe, he was only about ten blocks away from the hotel Dalton was holed up in, the walk would help get him into the mood of the Reach and free his mind from the corporate pressures, a sort of pre-contact meditation by soaking in his surroundings. John was enjoying this already.</span></span></span></span>

“Hurry up I want this door closed” said John,
Jim scooted past him into the building, he immediately saw that the door opened directly onto a set of stairs that went down into a basement. Jim Paused as John closed the door behind him with a heavy thud and punched in a code on the discreet keypad on the wall. 
Jim a few steps down hadn’t seen the keypad when he rushed in, suspiciously looked at it. John saw the look “Don’t worry Jim, just disabling the security system, the door doesn’t lock from this side, you can get out anytime you want.” He brushed past Jim and went down the stairs.
At the bottom of the stairs there was a small landing and another door, this one was just like a normal door, not the steel door to they just come through from the outside, John opened it and stepped inside without any fanfare.
Cautiously Jim followed John inside to the basement, looking around he could see this was nothing like the sparse second-hand set-up of the safe room out by the Scar that Vex had wanted him to stay in. 
The contrast couldn’t have been more stark, the main room they’d stepped into was well furnished with what looked like newly bought furniture, there was a set of large matching lounges around a large wall screen. The kitchen was large and well appointed almost professional, from where he was standing he could see bedrooms off to the side, in fact it looked a lot like a high end apartment, just without the windows.
John spoke up break Jim’s surveying “Ok, a quick tour and then I think you need a shower and some new clothes.”
Jim looked down at himself in the second hand clothes he’d been wearing for days now, he couldn’t disagree with that.
John continued and waved around the room they we’re standing in “Main lounge and kitchen, obviously, over there a couple of bedrooms, ensuite for each.” He moved towards a door that was on the opposite side of the room and opened the door.
“…and here this is the office I guess you’d call it” the room was stacked with computer racking along one wall and an commercial grade looking terminal on the other. Jim couldn’t help himself and whistled at the sight of the tech humming and blinking with tiny lights.
“Yep, its a pretty solid set-up, we can tap into just about anything, that’s kind of what we do down here. Do me a favour and don’t mess with anything in here, it’s not cheap and we can’t just go out and replace this stuff.”
Jim nodded and asked “Is that terminal connected to the grid?”
Almost boasting now, John answered “Sure is, but it’s kind of a one way system, it won’t allow inbound comms, like you can search around for anything you want, but it’ll cut you off if it thinks something is trying to reach back to you”
John flicked off the light and closed the door.
This place seemed too good to be true “So who are you really?” Jim asked.
“Like I said, we have mutual friends, but I’m not looking for you to do anything for me, I just want to keep you safe until you work out your next move and perhaps help if I can”
“So you know Vex?”
John, waved him off “No I don’t, but we don’t all know each other, that’s kind of the point though. Look I’ll answer more questions later, I’ve got a couple of urgent things to do right now that you’re here, not least of which is grab some supplies, the kitchen is empty and I wasn’t expecting guests, I’ll be back in a couple of hours.”
Jim didn’t think he’d really answered the questions, but he wasn’t forcing anything onto him right now, which was a welcome change. He decided that’d he’d take the comfort of a safe place for the night, a warm shower and a real bed.
John was halfway out the door and Jim called to him “You mentioned a code to get in?”
“That’s right I did” he reached into his pocked and pulled out a small plastic card and flipped it across the room the Jim, who caught expert throw easily
“That’s a prox card, it will open the door and disarm the alarm, just wave it on the door, but if I were you I’d be staying put for a while, it won’t take long for the incident a the store to hit mainstream and then everyone will be out to find you. Catch you later”
He closed the door to the stairs and left, Jim was alone again in someone else’s safe house. This was so different to the Grey’s he’d encountered before, clearly well funded and not the least bit afraid of technology like Vex and her crew. Was this a rich offshoot, or something altogether different, he’d find out one way of the other, but for now, a hot shower.</span></span></span></span>
