<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">ok, here's section 1 of chapter 17: Vex was pacing the room, silent with fury; no one dared to speak. The main room of the Grey’s safe house out in the scar territory was full this morning. Vex had demanded an unprecedented meeting of all of the Grey’s cell leaders. Normally a meeting like this was far too risky, but today Vex wanted answers and wasn’t about to waste time going through the normal communications channels.
Vex stopped pacing and spoke “How the fuck does a corporate executive, who’s been sitting behind desk and sipping wind for twenty year bust out of this safe house and then just disappear?”
No one answered.
Vex pointed at Corra “Just tell me how you fucked up so bad?”
Corra paled. “He caught me off guard, I didn’t think for one moment he would run”
“When did I ever tell you we made assumptions like that here? We can’t afford to. Now there’s a man out that in the city who knows my face, and the face of half the room here, and worse still he knows about this safe house. We don’t know where he is, or what he’ll do; if he gets caught by the CEB all of what we’ve worked for these last few year will be blown.” 
Again the room was silent; it was best not to give Vex a target when she was angry.
Vex started pacing again “Brask, you’re up; Rook is blown with Jim. I need you to find Jim, we can’t have him out there in the wild. I need you to find him fast, you just know the CEB is gunning for him too.”
Brask nodded “Got it, and when I find him?” the question hung heavy in the silence of the room.
Vex took a moment then answered “Bring him to me, I’ll talk to him. If he’s not on board with us; he can rot buried out in the Scar.”
Brask nodded again and got up to leave, he didn;t want to stay around for what was coming next. 
Vex watched him leave, deliberately not speaking until she knew he’d left the safe house. She turned to speak to Rook next; he was sitting at the kitchen table drinking a cooling synth coffee.
“Rook, you’re not dropping Jim completely; Brask has got the lead on him for now, but keep an eye out in case we can’t grab him and we have to go more, kinetic. You can go”, She dismissed him.
Again Vex waited until Rook left before continuing. She spoke to a man who was sitting in the shadows at the back of the room. She spoke with a level of respect no one had been afforded at the meeting so far.
“You need to get our new friend onboard with us quickly. We’re going to need access into Nova’s systems sooner rather than later.” Vex Said
The man answered “Are you sure? Right now he doesn’t know who I am. Besides, he’s no hacker.”
“I know but he’s got access to terminals that can get us what we need.”
“That was just a simple task, a mere theft, what you’re talking about is a serious hack.”
“I know, but with fucking Jim Dalton possibly blowing our whole organisations at any time, do we have any choice but to bring out plans forward?”
The man considered her statement “No, I don’t think we do” he paused and Vex waited for him to speak again “What about this place?” he asked.
Vex looked around at Corra and the three other people were left in the room. She raised her eyebrow to the man who quietly nodded.
Vex barked to the others in the room. “Ok, we’ve got to assume this place is burnt; pack it all up and make sure there’s nothing left but ashes when you’re done. Corra you and I can start downstairs.”
With that vex walked across the room and down the stairs, Corra followed happy to have been spared any more public dressing down.
The three people left in the room looked to the man still sitting in the back of the room. “You heard her, let’s not waste time”
They silently moved to different corners of the room and started unpacking cupboards and drawers; this was clearly something they’d practiced. 
A single gunshot rang out from downstairs; they all stopped dead in thier tracks. 
The man stood up and walked towards the stairs just as Vex came up them. She saw everyone staring at her and barked “Get on with it, we’ve got fifteen minutes before we’re all out of here.”</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">here's some new work, section2 of chapter 17: It was early in the morning and Neil was awake. It was too early actually; he’d been struggling to sleep ever since he’d seen his family and found out they’d all been deceived. He couldn’t put his finger on who or why would do that to him and it kept him up at nights trying to work the problem. If he was being honest with himself he was also nervous with anticipation
The street lights outside we’re seeping their yellow light through the curtains in the lounge of his meagre apartment in the half way house; the sun was just starting to light the sky. 
It was about thirty minutes before his alarm was going to go off and Neil was sprawled across the small two seat lounge watching the small TV bolted to the wall. The news of the day was another update on Jim Dalton.
“ …Dalton hasn’t been seen now for a least 4 days; despite hundreds of claimed sightings ranging from the Scar all the way across the to Reach. Metro Police remain concerned about his safety and are actively pursuing all leads. No words on the group called the Grey’s; they remain largely unknown. Metro Police are continuing to look into who is behind the group, but have not been able to pin the group down as yet…”
Neil flicked the mute button, he’d be following Jim Dlaton’s sotry closely, ever since the Grey’s had been tied to his downfall. He felt oddly special knowing the Grey’s personally and having done jobs for them; did that make him a Grey he wondered?
There was a quiet knock on the door. Neil looked at the door as if he could see through it a know who’d be knocking on his door so early in the morning. It was probably Grant, the safe house, manager checking up on him. 
Reluctantly he got up off the couch, stretched and sauntered over to the door, he was in no rush; whoever it was could wait. He stopped at the door an hesitated, the building was silent, did he imagine the knock?
The knock came again, just as quietly as before. He opened the door, it was Knox.
Neil was shocked, what was Knox doing here? He hadn’t really spoken to him for weeks; ever since he’d got settled in to his job really.
“Knox, what are you doing here, and so early?”
Knox smiled “Are you going to let me in?” he countered.
“Of course, come in. It’s not much buts it’s mine for only half my monthly allowance” Neil said dripping with sarcasm.
Knox chuckled as he moved inside “Yep, they haven’t changed much since I got out, my first place was pretty much the same.”
 “How long ago was that now?”
Knox sat at the small table “Must be at least ten years ago now.”
“Ten years, and still grinding it out with the rest of us our here, seems pretty rigged to me”
Knox nodded in agreement, and asked “you wouldn’t be able to make me a coffee, I had an early start and something makes me think this will be a long day.”
Neil moved over the small kitchenette and pulled out a jar of instant coffee. It was the best he could find in the loca area; he’d splurged a fair chunk of his left over credits for it. He’d figured if he had to live in this shit hole at least he could look forward a half decent coffee each morning.
Waiting for the kettle to boil he asked “Knox, its nice to see you, what the hell are you doing here at my place so damn early. Is it about my job?” Neil was starting to get worried that his escapade of a few days ago had been discovered.
“No, it’s not about your day job, but it is about a job of sorts”
“Knox you’re not making any sense.” Neil was very confused now.
The kettle boiled and Neil filled tow cups with hot water, the smell wafted up was almost like real coffee. Knox waited silently for Neil to sit at the table; he sipped at the steaming black coffee with his eyes closed savouring the warmth of the black liquid.
“I see you haven’t skimped on this, it’s the good stuff.” Knox sat forward and fixed his eyes onto Neil. this wasn’t the kind hearted man Neil thought he knew; the gaze was suddenly all business.
“Neil, remember when I told you to steer clear of Rook and his type?”
 “Yes” Neil said simply, he didn’t expect the conversation to go in this direction; he wasn’t sure he’d like it.
“Well, it seems like you didn’t listen to me and know they want you to do some more things for them.”
Neil was shocked “Wait, are you involved with them; did they send you here?”
Knox’s gaze didn’t move “Yes, and yes.”
“Fucking hell Knox, are you telling me you were one them from the start?”
“ Neil, under normal circumstances you’d never have known. This Jim Dalton that’s been all over the news has meant a change of plans; an acceleration if you will.”
Neil was floored, Knox the man who’d helped him out as a mentor showing him the ropes when he first started working was a Grey.
“Knox, I don;t know what to say.”
Knox smiled that disarming smile he had that made him look like a kind old man and said “You don’t have to say anything Neil, you have to do something. I believe last time you and Vex spoke you were ready for more work. We’ll, I’m here to give you your next job. Are you ready?”
This was not how he though this morning would go, but it was what he‘d been waiting for. The Greys had surprised him yet again; Neil was seriously impressed with how well they could keep doing that. These were people who could get stuff done and he was on board.
“I’m ready.”</span></span></span></span>

He didn’t know how long he slept, or what time it was; there were no windows in the bedroom. The only light in the room was softly leaking under the door from the main lounge and kitchen area outside the bedroom. 
He stretched and rolled around luxuriating in the comfort of the queen sized bed, a real actual bed, not some bunk or old couch. Jim never thought such simple pleasures of a warm bed and a full stomach could be so good.
He wasn’t ready to get up yet. There was no need to, no alarms schedules, no places he needed to go. In fact lying there basking in his immediate comfort, Jim could picture himself holed up in this basement for ever. 
He knew it was just a dream though. His eyes still closed unwilling to break the spell, he reflected on this latest turn of events. He was, for the time being, safely squirrelled away here. John had brought in enough supplies last night for at least a week along with a hot and fresh take-away meal from one of the many late night restaurants plying thier trade all night in the Reach.
He thought more about John, although he doubted that was him name. The man had stepped in at the last minute to rescue him, what a coincidence that John just happened to be in the store at the right time and had this basement hide-out nearby all ready to go. Jim didn’t think it was just luck that it all lined up for him so neatly, he filed that questions to growing list of things he didn’t understand.
Jim assumed John was connected to the Greys, although he had never really confirmed it. That was how they operated Jim thought; never directly answering anything. It was a tactic Jim was going to use more often now too.
He thought about what he could confirm; John didnt know Vex, which might be a good thing for Jim. He could see that this branch of the Greys seemed to have a lot more resources and were definitely not scared of technology, the commercial grade server set-up in this basement was evidence of that. 
He wondered how many other factions the Greys were out there? This world of underground resistance was all at once shocking and liberating at the same time.
One thing he did know was that John had shown him more respect and friendliness than any of the Vex’s Greys had, and he was going to soak up that hospitality until he knew what he was going to do next.
What was he going to do next he thought? He didn’t actually know, he’d been so busy surviving that thinking long-term had not even been on his radar, all he’d done was react and run. 
Today he was going to figure out a way to fight back, but first he was going to cook himself a big breakfast and brew a big hot mug of coffee or two. He opened his eyes , threw off the bedsheets and sat-up, all of a sudden invigorated by what lay ahead.</span></span></span></span>

John was back in the Nova Corp office building knowing Jim was safely locked away out on the Reach. Just like all members of Nova Corp’s Special Projects department, he has a small office on the 37th floor befitting his status as a Level 7 executive at Nova. The only concession to what he and the department actually did was that the whole floor was locked down tight, no one came in or out without permission from the very top, and that was never given.
It wasn’t too bad really, certainly it was a big step up after a decade at the Citizen Enforcement Bureau where he rode a worn down steel desk in a cold open plan office. He never had time to really concentrate there, it was a constant loud hum of voices, agents chasing down leads, citizens pleading for just one more chance and they’d stay on the right side of the law; they never did so he stopped giving chances. 
Here at Nova he had an office to himself, it was small, but not tiny and it was his own, in keeping with Nova’s policy you could decorated it however you wanted and on this floor there was no budget. John had decided to go for an old school lawyers look, dark faux wood and leather, it was a luxury bolt hole when he need to work on projects. He figured he deserved it after years serving the people, he never once regretted jumping ship to the private sector.
Not that he didn’t still like getting out in the field getting his hands dirty for Nova, but some days it was a hard choice, stay put in comfort and send a junior operator, or schlep outside and muscle some unknowing citizen into playing some small part in one of Nova’s grand projects. 
Jim Dalton wasn’t any ordinary dupe though, he’d proven time and again he could get the better of even one of the best resourced departments, he just wouldn’t stay inside the lines they’d very carefully drawn for him. 
Rob stopped by a poked his head into John’s office.
“You’re back, good, what’s Daltons status?” Rob asked.
“He’s locked up in one of our data scoop bunkers out in the Reach, he’s probably worked out by now he can’t get out, but I’ve stocked it for a least a week so we have time to make out next move.”
“Good work, I’ll come back to you once we know what we want to do with him, I’ve got a call with the boss later and we’ll decide if we need to end the project or not” Rob said.
“Yes Sir, I’ll be ready” responded John in his usual matter of fact way.
“Ok, I’m out to lunch, be back later” said Ron as he walked away without bothering to hear if John answered him of not. John didn’t answer just looked at Rob’s back as he left. If Rob had looked back he would have seen a predatory smile on John’s face as he realised that Rob just didn’t know how to deal with the problem and that was leverage John thought he could use.</span></span></span></span>
